entities.name: Alonso Suárez de la Fuente del Sauce
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Alonso Suárez de la Fuente del Sauce (1450–1520) was a prominent Castilian Roman Catholic prelate whose ecclesiastical career spanned the pivotal transition from the late Reconquista era to the early consolidation of the unified Spanish monarchy under the Catholic Monarchs, Ferdinand II of Aragon and Isabella I of Castile. As Bishop of Mondoñedo (1493–1496), Lugo (1496–1500), and most significantly, Jaén (1500–1520), he played a crucial administrative and spiritual role in the newly established political and religious order of the nascent Spanish state. His tenure in Jaén, a strategically vital diocese bordering the recently conquered Nasrid Kingdom of Granada, placed him at the forefront of the crown's efforts to integrate former frontier territories and solidify Catholic hegemony in Southern Spain during the initial decades of the 16th century.

Suárez de la Fuente del Sauce's ascent through the ecclesiastical ranks began in the final years of the 15th century, culminating in his appointment to the influential See of Jaén in 1500, a position he held for two decades until his death on November 15, 1520. During his episcopacy in Jaén, he was instrumental in the administrative reorganization of the diocese, which had only recently been secured from Muslim rule, and oversaw the spiritual and social integration of its diverse populace. He actively supported the construction and embellishment of churches and religious institutions, contributing to the Christianization and Castilianization of the region. His administrative prowess was also evident in his involvement in the broader ecclesiastical councils and affairs of the Spanish Church, aligning diocesan practices with the reforms advocated by the Catholic Monarchs.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Alonso Suárez de la Fuente del Sauce's two-decade episcopacy in Jaén was critical for the administrative and spiritual consolidation of a key frontier region into the unified Spanish Catholic state following the Reconquista. His efforts helped solidify the religious and political landscape of Southern Spain for centuries to come.
